claims.statement: The FastAPI application composes dashboard, plan, workflow approval, Linear (MDA channel), Slack, GitHub, Notion, and health/completion routers; it validates CORS configuration to reject wildcard origins when credentials are enabled, and its lifespan startup validates sandbox provider, local-development LLM model, and Slack configuration before serving.
GitHub and Slack webhook routes verify their platform signature against the raw request body before JSON parsing and return HTTP 401 when verification fails.
Slack message delivery is deduplicated by claiming the event id before the normal background task is scheduled, so only a claimed event can create a Slack run.
Slack blocks operations in externally shared or unverified channels; an app mention in an external shared channel receives a claimed one-time refusal reply and is not dispatched.
Outside code channels, Slack only admits ordinary messages directed at Open SWE through a mention, DM, ready-plan reply, or qualifying untagged two-party reply, and it drops bot/self messages.
Slack resolves a location by preferring an explicit mapping, then metadata matches, then a deterministic id; a conflicting explicit mapping is surfaced as an error rather than guessed.
Slack processing requires a valid mapped user GitHub token unless bot-token-only mode is enabled, and prompts the user to link or re-authenticate instead of dispatching when the token is unavailable.
Slack sends explicit requests with multitask_strategy='interrupt' and other follow-ups with 'enqueue'; message edits are queued rather than dispatched as standalone runs.

Linear integration uses an MDA channel that handles session lifecycle and authentication, declining sessions when the author lacks repository access or has not linked their GitHub account, and starting runs on deterministic threads with channel metadata marking.

A Linear session establishes a run thread with system issue context, human comment messages, handles image URL vision-model fallback, dispatches with a completion webhook, and posts a trace reply in the Linear conversation.

GitHub routes multiplex issue, PR, comment, review, push, and CI events, filter unsupported actions, apply repository/organization gates, require mentions for ordinary issue/comment work, and route review-finding replies separately.

GitHub PR comment processing recovers an embedded Open SWE branch UUID when present and otherwise derives a PR thread id, resolves the user's token with one 401 refresh retry, reacts with eyes, serializes comments since the last tag, and dispatches them.
Reviewer runs use reviewer_thread_id and assistant_id='reviewer', separating auto-review and re-review work from the coding-agent thread and graph.

The dashboard allows lazy creation only for run.start, enriches it with authenticated-user attribution, normalized configuration and structured input, while active-thread dashboard messages are queued and cancellation interrupts all live runs on the thread.

Desktop execution happens through a bridge (sandbox) bound to a thread; a thread can be moved to a machine running the desktop CLI via worktree handoff, after which downstream execution validates only allowlisted local projects or worktrees under the configured root are accessed.

Schedules are represented by LangGraph crons targeting the scheduler assistant; a schedule tick creates a fresh UUID thread after obtaining schedule/automation metadata and rechecking the creator's repository access.
Thread-id derivations are a persisted cross-process routing contract, so changing their namespaces or input strings can orphan live threads.

Input serialization enforces human/system kind alignment, XML-escapes authored content in input-message envelopes, and uses SHA-256-hashed dynamic context introductions with untrusted channel topic/purpose fields marked trust='untrusted'.
dispatch_agent_run rejects mixing a prebuilt input with raw content or identities, otherwise constructs input as needed and delegates all agent/reviewer triggers to create_durable_run.

create_durable_run defaults to interrupt multitasking, async durability, resumable streaming, Protocol v2 stream configuration and subgraphs via V3_RUN_STREAM_MODES, and correlates configurable state and metadata with invocation_id (legacy prepare_run_id alias).
A completion webhook is attached only when its secret is configured and its URL is absolute and non-loopback; the receiving health route fails closed on the token.

Run completion schedules eligible successful Slack cost refreshes and, for error or timeout, performs best-effort reviewer/code-channel cleanup and source-specific failure replies with per-run idempotence; interrupted runs are not failure replies.

RunInput is a TypedDict with required messages list (role, content, optional id per message) and optional files dict; it is the gateway contract all invocation sources must satisfy before LangGraph dispatch.

InputMessageContext is a TypedDict envelope for a single message: sender_id, surface, kind (human or system), optional channel_id, and optional structured data; it is combined with Identity objects to construct serialized input.

PersonIdentity, ChannelIdentity, and SystemIdentity are namespaced TypedDicts that carry cross-surface metadata and are deduplicated by SHA-256 content hash so unchanged identities are not re-injected on later turns.

create_durable_run marks every run with __event_streaming_v2 protocol marker for v2 streaming, attaches Protocol v2 stream modes (values, updates, messages, custom, tasks, checkpoints) and subgraphs, enabling tools events and nested-agent visibility for externally triggered runs.

Multitask strategy interrupt halts the active run while preserving its checkpoints, resuming the agent with full history plus the new message; enqueue queues sequential processing after the active run completes.

Completion webhook degrades gracefully: if COMPLETION_WEBHOOK_URL is relative or loopback, dispatch omits the webhook rather than failing run creation, logging a warning so operators notice misconfiguration.
